title: 21st Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 9:01 with the day's agenda and a question session for the Minister of Dhivehi Language, Culture and Heritage, Adam Naseer Ibrahim. Members asked about repairs to Hukuru Miskiy, the Kalhuoffummi ship replica park, heritage sites in their constituencies, the Dhivehi language and national days, and the minister said heritage policy now aims at protection plus income. Two committee reports followed (non-resident ambassador nominations, and a Civil Service Commission nominee) and all four appointments were then approved 71-0 in recorded votes. The next sitting was set for Monday 21 April 2025 at 9:00. This part contains only the electronic voting records appended to the minutes, with no spoken debate. It shows four open votes on appointments: the member-by-member tables for the proposed non-resident ambassador to Sweden, then the proposed ambassadors to Seychelles and Austria, and the proposed Civil Service Commission member. In each vote 76 members were present, 75 were eligible to vote, 71 voted yes, none voted no or abstained, and 4 did not vote.

speakers.name: Adam Naseer Ibrahim
positions: Said Hukuru Miskiy works stopped after mid-2023 and described damage to the building; said the Kalhuoffummi park is being redesigned as a digital museum.
Said heritage policy is to protect sites while earning income, citing a Baarashu and Thakandhoo project whose first phase could open by National Day.
Said an oral history project, a Dhivehi national identity project and research on atoll dialects are underway.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked when work on the Hukuru Miskiy restoration will restart and finish, given damage to the building.
Asked which heritage sites the minister has restored since taking office.
Asked when the Kalhuoffummi park will reopen after months of closure.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked what work the national heritage research centre is currently doing.
Told the opposition to avoid bringing questions he saw as unnecessary, and said he had no question for the minister.
Backed the ambassador report and defended the pace and workload of the Majlis and its committees.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked what the previous government did for Fuvahmulah's heritage sites and what is planned.
Asked what the ministry is doing to develop and teach the Fuvahmulah dialect.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked about heritage sites in Vaikaradhoo, Neylaidhoo and Kurinbi and how love of heritage can be built in people.
Backed the report but raised concern that the Majlis is moving faster than the government, citing delayed NSPA therapy payments.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Asked about the ruined Darul Aathaar building and the Landhoo kitchen site museum, and what the previous government did for heritage sites.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Asked whether the ministry's spending delivers benefits to the Maldivian public in proportion to the cost.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Asked what the ministry is doing to keep Dhivehi as children's mother tongue, noting many young children speak a foreign language.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Asked for clarity on how far the Landhoo site museum project has progressed, and how well the previous government preserved sites.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked whether the minister has visited Addu City heritage sites and whether studies and development plans exist for them.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked about the Lily Haus project in Kelaa, how it was changed after handover, and how much was spent.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked why the Hukuru Miskiy grounds are decaying and what plans exist to protect the Thoddoo Daagaba site.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Asked how much the previous government spent on the Hukuru Miskiy railings.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Asked what plan exists for Huraa, given its links to Sultan Hassan Izzuddin and its natural beauty.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Asked how the protected island of Mathee in the reef will be repaired, and whether the Kalhuvakaru mosque was ever lost.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked how the ministry will protect Addu's heritage, including the Gan site left by the British.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Asked whether there is a plan for a special building in Ihavandhoo honouring Thakurufaanu's mother.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Asked how the national identity project will directly benefit Maldivians and what the ministry's plan is for heritage change.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Asked the minister's view of the importance of having a ministry for language, culture and heritage.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Asked whether the old Boduatige house will be repaired, noting repeated announcements and asking about budget plans.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Asked whether a list of artists is being prepared and whether the Tharijehige house in Kulhudhuffushi will be protected.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked about repairing the decayed Thinadhoo museum park, the old mosque foundation, and protecting the lathe iron.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked what the ministry is doing in Laamu Atoll and whether any income has actually been earned from the new policy.

speakers.name: Hassan Waheed
positions: Asked how far the Dhonhiyala and Aliffulu legends have been studied and what is being done for the Diyamigili site.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Asked how national days will be marked and revived, including in schools.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Asked whether the ministry is working to earn income from culture and heritage in tourist islands like Thulusdhoo.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Asked whether the Kalhuvakaru mosque area is closed to visitors and whether the Kalhuoffummi was sealed to its original dimensions.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shamin Habeeb
positions: Asked what plan exists to protect the Kurendhoo Loi Ziyaarath and whether the ministry will support tourism use.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked about restoration work done on heritage sites and under what legal power a political appointee heads the Dhivehi Language Academy.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Presented the Foreign Relations Committee report finding the nominees for Sweden, Seychelles and Austria meet the legal requirements.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Presented the committee report finding nominee Mohamed Mujthaz met the requirements, scoring an average of 88.11 percent, with no public complaints.

decisions: Aishath Shaan Shakir approved as non-resident ambassador to the Kingdom of Sweden.
Masood Imad approved as non-resident ambassador to the Republic of Seychelles.
Dr. Salma Rasheed approved as non-resident ambassador to the Republic of Austria.
Mohamed Mujthaz approved as a member of the Civil Service Commission.
Next sitting set for Monday 21 April 2025 at 9:00.
Aishath Shaan Shakir's appointment as non-resident ambassador to Sweden received 71 yes votes, none against.
Masood Imad's appointment as non-resident ambassador to Seychelles received 71 yes votes, none against.
Dr. Salma Rasheed's appointment as non-resident ambassador to Austria received 71 yes votes, none against.
Mohamed Mujuthaz's appointment as Civil Service Commission member received 71 yes votes, none against.
